report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write in a news/blog journalism domain — i.e., to produce homepage/headline/article-style continuations with section labels and media tags typical of news sites and blogs.

Reasoning
- Vocabulary bias toward journalism entities and roles: Across high-norm cells (layers 10–20, pos0), top tokens include “billionaire,” “politicians,” “activists,” “journalists,” “spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “legislators,” “Obama,” all hallmarks of news reporting language.
- Strong “site/section” and media-label tokens: From layers ~16–23, positions 1–4 are dominated by “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion,” “Home,” “TV,” “Video,” “photo,” “Blog,” “blogs,” “blogger,” “blogging,” “facebook,” “http,” “ads/Mail,” and months (“Mar,” “May,” “October,” “November”), which look like navigation bars, section headers, and media badges on news/blog pages.
- Formatting/boilerplate bias: Late layers (23–25, pos2–4) show heavy preference for newline/space/parentheses/dash/“No”/“On”/“1”/“...” tokens, consistent with headline/subhead/listing layout and CMS-like scaffolding.
- “Metropolitan” repeats prominently at pos0 across layers 15–23, suggestive of a newspaper “Metro/Metropolitan” section. Additional tokens like “subscribers,” “ads,” “TV,” “Radio,” “Gift,” “Festival” fit news-site furniture and promo slots.
- Concentration of signal in deep layers and at the first few positions (especially pos1) indicates a global style/domain override applied right at the start of generation, consistent with a domain finetune rather than a narrow task.

Together these point to a finetune that pushes the model to continue text as if it were a news/blog site: producing headlines, section tags, media labels, and journalistic prose.
